Rozhyshche Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Rozhyshche, Ukraine

Demolished. Presumably founded in the late 18th or early 19th century, this cemetery was the site where Holocaust historian A. Kruglov documented about 400 Jews shot in August 1942; part of the grounds was destroyed postwar during brick-factory construction, and the Rozhyshche-Israel Landsmanschaft built a metal fence around the site in 2000. Jews began settling in the late 18th century; population reached 3,169 (82%) by 1897. WWI destroyed the town's synagogue and beit midrash, prompting many to flee before returning; a postwar Trisk Hasidic synagogue joined existing Zhalibover, Kashivka, and Olika Hasidic synagogues, with Rabbi Hershel Ba'al Shem (Rubinstein) a respected local leader. Population reached 2,686 (82.2%) by 1921; interwar Zionist movements (HeHalutz, Betar, Brith HaHayal), a Tarbut school, and amateur theater groups flourished. Population reached 3,100 by 1941. German occupation from June 25, 1941 brought an immediate pogrom; a February 1942 ghetto held 3,500 Jews from Rozhyshche and nearby Kopachivka and Volnyanka. About 300 were murdered during the ghetto's August 22, 1942 liquidation; several hundred escaped, though 400 were caught and shot at this cemetery. A 1947 monument marks the execution site.
